transcript.content: Hi, it's good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Oh, um… thank you. I’m probably making more of it than I should, but I’ve been getting quite unsettled at work. I’m a teacher, and lately I can’t seem to shake the feeling that some staff emails, and even the morning announcements, have… sort of hidden meanings about me.

My colleagues have been kind and they’ve shown me the emails went to everyone, so I do understand that. It’s just that the feeling doesn’t quite go away, and it’s been bothering me enough that I thought I should talk to someone. Does that make sense?
Right now, do you believe those emails and announcements really are about you?

I… I don’t want to sound unreasonable. Part of me knows they’re sent to everyone, because people have shown me that. But yes, in the moment it really does feel like certain emails or announcements are… coded somehow, like they’re referring to me. I can’t quite shake that feeling, even though I’m trying to be sensible about it.
When you have that feeling, are you able to tell yourself it’s probably not true, or does it feel completely certain that the messages are about you?

I can sometimes tell myself it’s probably not true, yes… especially if someone shows me the email went to everyone. I don’t think I’m completely certain all the time.

But when it’s happening, it feels very convincing—like there’s something in the wording or the timing that’s meant for me. I know that may sound a bit silly, and I do try to talk myself out of it, but the feeling still lingers.
Have you been hearing voices when no one else is there?

Um… not often. I mean, I wouldn’t want to make it sound worse than it is.

But yes, sometimes when the house is very quiet, or after my classroom has emptied, I’ll hear a woman’s voice say my name, or just make a short comment about what I’m doing. It’s clear enough that I’ve actually answered before realizing there isn’t anyone there.

That… that is the sort of thing you mean, isn’t it?
When you hear that woman’s voice, does it ever comment on what you’re doing as it happens?

Yes… sometimes. Not like a running commentary or anything, I don’t think. It’s usually just a brief thing, like a woman’s voice saying my name, or making a small comment about what I’m doing.

It tends to happen when it’s very quiet at home, or after the classroom has emptied. It can be clear enough that I answer, and then I realize no one is actually there. I know that sounds odd… but that’s what happens.
Have there been times when your mood was unusually high or overly energetic?

I don’t think so, no… not unusually high. I have days where I feel a bit more capable, or I get more done if I’ve slept well, but I wouldn’t say overly energetic.

Unless you mean something quite specific? I don’t think I’ve had anything like that, but I’m not sure I’m describing it the right way.
Have you found yourself becoming noticeably less interested in spending time with other people than you used to be?

A little, yes… though I don’t want to make it sound as if I don’t care about people, because I do. I still care about my students, and my friends.

It’s more that, for months now, the warmth or the drive to actually do things with people has sort of… drained away. I’ve let book club slide, and theater planning, and even just returning phone calls. If someone really pushes me, I’ll usually manage it, but left to myself I tend to let it go.

Does that answer what you mean?
About how long have you been hearing that woman’s voice?

I suppose… about four months now. Not constantly, really, and I don’t want to overstate it, but that’s roughly when I first noticed the woman’s voice — the one I sometimes answer before realizing no one’s there. Does that sound like the sort of timeframe you mean?
Did these experiences begin suddenly, over a few days, or did they come on gradually?

I think it was more gradual. It’s hard to pin down an exact start, but the overall change in how I’m thinking, working, and keeping up with people has been there since my youngest left for college… so, about a year and two months ago.

It wasn’t like one week everything changed. More like I kept telling myself it was just adjusting, or an empty-house sort of thing. Does that make sense?
Has there been a stretch of at least one month when these unusual experiences were happening regularly?

Yes… I think so. I mean, not every single day, but the worries about coded messages and the woman’s voice I sometimes answer have been going on regularly enough for about four months now.

I’m not sure if that counts the way you mean, but it’s definitely been longer than a month.
Since these experiences began, has your ability to do your job or take care of yourself become noticeably worse?

I’m still teaching, yes, so I wouldn’t want to make it sound like I’ve completely fallen apart. But… I suppose it has gotten harder.

I’ve had to lean on coworkers more than I used to — having them cover parts of project lessons, or help me get through planning meetings when I’m not quite keeping up. And outside of work, I’ve become less reliable than I’d like. I’ve stopped really showing up for book club, theater things, neighborhood events… I keep meaning to, but I don’t follow through.

So yes, I guess noticeably worse, though I’m still managing in some ways. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
